supportsMassMediaCo: Mass Media Co. (MMC) provides data-driven digital marketing services, using real-time data to make decisions. Its secure audience database holds verified personally identifiable information (PII), which lets MMC build highly targeted campaigns.

Scope (quote exactly): 'product revamp, user interviews, information architecture (IA), UI and UX design, and web and mobile app design.' (Print the scope with '(IA)' only inside this exact quote, or drop '(IA)': see entityNotes.)

Challenge: the team used several systems separately; no consistent user experience; order takers struggled to move between disconnected systems to fulfill customer orders; the process would not scale.

Approach: a discovery workshop with MMC stakeholders and users covering product definition, strategy, information architecture and user flows; result: an omnichannel platform built around five experiences: social media sales (social campaigns such as Facebook marketing packaged as products with goals), campaign sales creation (revenue, cost, total and order count at a glance), audience engagement reports (reach by device, age group and channel), task management (owner, due date, progress per creative task), product and order management (order summary across email, audio, video and H&V channels).

Solution: task management dashboard (sales operations, open tasks, task flow by client, recent tasks); order management (build an order from data products, digital channels and data processing services with the estimated cost shown as they go); advanced data analytics for audience segmentation; real-time performance tracking.

Results (quote exactly, framed as reported results, never attributed to design alone): '30% increase in order processing efficiency'; '53% increase in audience engagement'; '3% improvement in task completion'. Do not use the '2+' error-rate line.

Images (reuse with case alt text and captions only): /work/mass-media-co/cover.webp ('The Mass Media Co. platform'), social-sales.webp ('Social media sales packages'), campaign-sales.webp ('Campaign sales at a glance'), audience-report.webp ('Audience engagement report'), task-cards.webp ('Task progress cards'), order-summary.webp ('Order summary by channel'), task-dashboard.webp ('Task management dashboard'), order-management.webp ('Order management').
supportsVocable: Vocable brings content operations into a single platform, centralizing the content lifecycle from ideation to optimization; founder Iman Oubou.
Scope (quote exactly): 'idea to product, stakeholder interviews, MVP launch strategy, UI and UX design, web app, and product enhancements.'
Challenge: researching trends took hours; measuring performance across tools was overwhelming; little time left for planning.

Designed: one editor with multiple AI models (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Meta); an idea and headline generator; the full creator journey mapped from stakeholder interviews (planning, drafting, optimizing, publishing); content templates (articles, descriptions, emails, press releases); a built-in keyword research tool; a dashboard with documents completed and in progress, active campaigns and a content plan; an editor with content score, readability and SEO checks and collaborators in the same document.

outline.h2: What makes UX design for media companies different?
outline.answerHint: Bold: UI UX design for media companies has to join tools that grew up separately, serve internal teams and their clients at once, and handle audience data with care. 4 cards, 1–2 sentences each. Write in new words.
points: Disconnected systems: MMC's order takers moved between separate systems to fulfill one customer order; the fix is one workflow, not prettier screens.

Internal teams and clients on one platform: order takers, sales teams and creative teams work inside; clients read audience engagement reports. Each role gets its own view and permissions (web app hub: user roles and permission states).

outline.h2: Which privacy and advertising standards shape media UI/UX design services?
outline.format: list (plain-string items; the H2 keeps the word 'standards')
outline.answerHint: Bold: four privacy, advertising and accessibility standards shape media UI/UX design services, and each one changes what media and marketing teams see on screen. Each item = one fact + its effect on screens + the primary link from externalSources. Closing line: we design to these standards; legal compliance stays with the client. Fact-checker verifies every rule before publishing.
points: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 level AA: keyboard access, visible focus and 4.5:1 contrast for normal-size text; colour is never the only way to convey information (success criterion 1.4.1), so audience charts and campaign status also carry labels.

California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), as amended by the CPRA: consumers can opt out of the sale or sharing of their personal information, and businesses must honor opt-out preference signals such as Global Privacy Control. Effect: audience data tools show each segment's opt-out status and keep opted-out records out of campaign builds.

Federal Trade Commission (FTC) native advertising guidance (Enforcement Policy Statement on Deceptively Formatted Advertisements and the 'Native Advertising: A Guide for Businesses'): ads must be identifiable as ads. Effect: sponsored content labels sit next to the content, in plain words, on every screen and template where it appears.

CAN-SPAM Act: commercial email needs a clear way to opt out, a valid physical postal address, and opt-outs honored within 10 business days. Effect: the email channel in order and campaign builders includes the unsubscribe and sender details by default.

outline.h2: FAQs about media UI/UX design services
outline.answerHint: Bold: these answers cover the 6 questions media and marketing companies ask most before hiring media UI/UX design services.
points: see faqs[]

faqs.q: Have you designed software for a media company?
faqs.a: Yes. For Mass Media Co., a data-driven digital marketing services company, we revamped separate order-taking systems into one omnichannel platform for social media sales, campaign sales, audience engagement reports, task management and order management; it reports a 30% increase in order processing efficiency. Link /case-studies/mass-media-co/. One media client: do not pluralise; Vocable may follow as 'a content marketing platform'.

faqs.q: Do you build the platform or write the code?
faqs.a: No. Our designers deliver annotated Figma files, design tokens and component specs, and your engineers write the code, including ad-tech, CRM and data integrations. (Matches the hub's 'designers do not write code'; answers the proxy questions 'Can you also develop the media product?' and 'Do UX/UI designers need to know how to code?').

faqs.q: Can you redesign media tools that are already in use?
faqs.a: Yes. Start with a UX audit of the live tools, $5,000–$15,000 over 2–3 weeks: heuristic evaluation, analytics review and a WCAG 2.2 level AA check, ending in a prioritized fix roadmap. A phased redesign then starts with the highest-traffic workflow, for example order management, and ships one workflow per release (web-app hub wording). Link /services/ux-audit-services/ only if the cost section did not already link it; else no link.

faqs.q: How long do media UI/UX design services take?
faqs.a: A UX audit takes 2–3 weeks, a design sprint for one surface such as the audience dashboard takes 4–8 weeks, and a full media platform design takes 8–16 weeks (40–80 working days). Home.ts and hub figures only.

faqs.q: Do you design reader or subscriber apps for publishers?
faqs.a: Yes, as mobile and web app design: reader apps, subscription flows and video or audio players follow the same 5 steps through our mobile app UI UX design services (link /services/mobile-app-ui-ux-design-services/). Our published media work so far is Mass Media Co.'s order, campaign and reporting platform (its scope included web and mobile app design), so we do not claim reader apps, paywalls or newsroom tools as past work.

faqs.q: Can better UX design increase audience engagement on a media platform?
faqs.a: Yes, as one factor among several. On the platform we designed for Mass Media Co., the company reports a 53% increase in audience engagement alongside a 30% increase in order processing efficiency; data, campaigns and client support shaped those results too, so we do not attribute them to design alone. Answers the proxy questions on engagement and monetization.
